---
title: "Proof-like blocks keep the LaTeX style in the simple appearance"
format: typst
keep-typ: true
_quarto:
  tests:
    typst:
      ensureTypstFileRegexMatches:
        -
          # the header is italic and the body upright, as in LaTeX and HTML
          - '#let simple-proof-render\(prefix: none, title: "", full-title: auto, body\) = \{(\r\n?|\n)\s*emph\(prefix\)'
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"proof",(\r\n?|\n)\s*"Proof",'
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"remark",(\r\n?|\n)\s*"Remark",'
          - '#proof\(number: "", get-prefix: \(\.\.args\) => "Proof"\)\['
          # theorems keep the bold header
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"theorem",(\r\n?|\n)\s*text\(weight: "bold", "Theorem"\),'
          # attributes on the block still reach the output
          - '#block\(fill: yellow\)\[(\r\n?|\n)#set text\(fill: red\);(\r\n?|\n)#proof\('
        -
          - 'text\(weight: "bold", "Proof"\)'
          - 'text\(weight: "bold", "Remark"\)'
      ensurePdfRegexMatches:
        -
          - 'Remark 1 \(Named\)\. A numbered remark'
          - 'Proof\. An unnumbered proof'
        - []
---

In the `simple` appearance, which the documentation describes as classic
LaTeX style, `proof`, `remark` and `solution` headers are italic with an
upright body, as amsthm and the HTML output write them. Theorems keep a bold
header. A `style` attribute on the block still reaches the Typst output.

::: {#thm-a}
A theorem.
:::

::: {.proof}
An unnumbered proof.
:::

::: {#rem-a}
## Named
A numbered remark.
:::

::: {.proof style="background-color: yellow; color: red"}
A styled proof.
:::

See @rem-a.
